generation_mode: Reference-based complex reconstruction followed by targeted contour-junction finishing.
design: Asymmetric interlacing rounded-rhombus and superellipse phase families, broad mint fields, multiple apertures, controlled saddle junctions and varied contour widths.

prompts.prompt:
Create a NEW fully redrawn complex geometric artwork inspired by reference image 1. The reference establishes the visual language and level of complexity ONLY; do not trace its exact paths or copy its malformed intersections. Make visibly newly constructed geometry.

Panoramic 2:1 website background. Quiet pale dusty-lilac field over the left half. On the right: a sophisticated, DENSELY INTERLACED optical field of shifted rounded rhombi and elongated superellipse bands, extending beyond the top, right and bottom frame. Preserve the original's rich asymmetric geometry, broad diagonal mint fields, nested lavender contours, slender citron phase accents, curved diamond-shaped openings, narrow saddle connections and softly shaded planar surfaces.

Build THREE coordinated phase-shifted contour families, with slight relative rotations and different large scales. Their paths interact to create a large off-center rounded-diamond aperture toward the middle-right, two smaller asymmetric diamond/lens openings in the adjacent upper-left and lower-right portions of the patterned area, and expressive diagonal corridors connecting the regions. The forms belong to one continuous complex structure. Preserve broad areas alternating with purposeful narrow necks. The bands are NOT concentric with one another; their shifting centers and rotations are the source of the intricate pattern.

Resolve the interlacing rigorously: every visible broad band follows a continuous, smoothly curving trajectory across the field. Design clean crossing zones with a clear whole-surface foreground/background order, softly curved saddle gaps and precise pale-lilac separators. Underpassing contours resume with matching tangents and a coherent width on the other side. Color accents follow real boundaries and never become loose fragments. Think of carefully modeled parametric optical art, professionally drafted and inspected, with elegant controlled complex curves. Each bend, opening, taper and crossing is intentional. Keep all contours finished; broad shapes must not arbitrarily collapse into little spikes.

Use broad muted violet and lavender planes (#a78bbd, #b7a4ce), large muted mint-teal sections (#a0c6be), restrained pale citron (#e8edba) and lilac negative-space channels (#ddd4e8). Gentle smooth gradients remain within individual color planes; edges are crisp and readable. The image is FLAT geometric editorial art, not a sculpture. No grain, texture, blur, vague fog, cast shadows, extruded walls or glossy materials.

ESSENTIAL: retain complex overlapping multi-phase geometry. Never simplify into separate identical diamond tiles, regular concentric rings, a ring chain, simple chevrons or a plain sinusoidal stripe. Rebuild the actual topology rather than merely sharpening the reference. No wavy accidental edges, broken contours, unfinished wedges, tangles, near-touching accidental seams, needle tips, stray slivers, warped corners, random decoration, text, logos, watermark, border or interface.

Input image 1 is the edit target. KEEP this rich asymmetric interwoven geometry, all three diamond/lens openings, broad mint fields, nested violet forms, varied contour widths, diagonal passages, exact panoramic composition and pastel palette. Do not simplify, rearrange, regularize or replace any major motif.

Make one precise finishing pass on the contour topology, like an expert parametric graphic designer refining the spline construction. Preserve the complexity and every important layer.

The visible image is approximately 1774 x 887. In particular:
1. Near 65% width / 38% height, at the upper-left inner flank of the large central aperture, the mint contour currently has a short isolated-looking capped/tapered end. Reconstruct this as a coherent continuation belonging to the complete mint surface around the main aperture. It should either continue visibly around the corner with a smooth clean boundary, or pass unambiguously behind the adjacent violet/citron band and resume on the same trajectory. No exposed dead-end, dangling tongue or free tip inside a lilac field.
2. Near 58–64% width / 15–28% height, where the smaller upper-left opening meets the broad upper mint plane and diagonal citron path, resolve all boundaries into ONE coherent crossing with a clear front/back order and tangent-continuous paths. Keep that smaller opening. Remove stray wedges, split tips, skinny fragments and nearly-touching edges. Preserve the broad planes and real phase-shift geometry.
3. Near 78–82% width / 80–86% height, finish the lower central saddle junction. Preserve the narrow lilac diamond-shaped gap and the diverging citron/violet contours, but make their curves meet the surrounding geometry in a controlled deliberate way. Clean continuous separation, no fused blob, accidental notch or razor-thin leftover.

Inspect the other intersections with the same rule: every colored surface has a complete clean closed boundary; every path is visibly continuous or clearly occluded by another whole surface. Hidden contours resume with matching tangents. All narrow accents remain attached to genuine geometric boundaries. Smooth gradients stay inside the planes, crisp antialiased edges, uniform pale-lilac empty left area. Keep broad-to-narrow phase variation and layered optical richness.

No new objects, no repeated tile system, no simple rings, no flattened concentric target, no separate icons, no loss of contour layers, no texture, grain, blur, 3D extrusion, shadows, text, logos or watermark. Change only unresolved contour junctions and surface-boundary finishing.
